docs.title: ZodKmp: Kotlin Multiplatform Validation
docs.text: ZodKmp is a Kotlin Multiplatform implementation of the popular Zod TypeScript validation library. It provides a declarative, type-safe way to validate data in your Kotlin Multiplatform projects.

docs.title: Platform Support
docs.text:
ZodKmp supports the following platforms:

  • Android (JVM)
  • iOS (Native)
  • JVM
  • JS (JavaScript)
  • Native (Linux, Windows, macOS)

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• ✅ Declarative Schema Definition - Define validation rules upfront
  • ✅ Compile-Time Safety - Schemas build on Kotlin's strong type system with type-safe outputs
  • ✅ Immutable Architecture - Immutable schemas that return new instances
  • ✅ Kotlin Multiplatform - Works on Android, iOS, and other Kotlin targets
  • ✅ Comprehensive API - Supports all major Zod validation features
  • ✅ Extensible - Easy to extend with custom validations
  • ✅ Minimal Dependencies - Single lightweight dependency (kotlinx-datetime)
  • ✅ Excellent Error Messages - Detailed, customizable error reporting

docs.title: Gradle
docs.text:
Add the following to your build.gradle.kts:

kotlin {
    sourceSets {
        val commonMain by getting {
            dependencies {
                implementation("io.github.piashcse:zodkmp:2.0.0")
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.text:

[libraries]

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
ZodKmp allows you to define validation schemas and use them to validate data:

import com.piashcse.zodkmp.Zod

// Define a schema
val userSchema = Zod.objectSchema<User>({
    string("name", Zod.string().min(2))
    string("email", Zod.string().email())
    number("age", Zod.number().min(0.0).max(120.0))
}) { map ->
    User(
        name = map["name"] as String,
        email = map["email"] as String,
        age = map["age"] as Double
    )
}

// Use the schema
val userData = mapOf(
    "name" to "John Doe",
    "email" to "john@example.com",
    "age" to 30.0
)

val result = userSchema.safeParse(userData)
when (result) {
    is ZodResult.Success -> println("Valid user: ${result.data}")
    is ZodResult.Failure -> println("Validation errors: ${result.error.errors}")
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
ZodKmp provides detailed error information:

val userSchema = Zod.objectSchema<User>({
    string("name", Zod.string().min(2))
    string("email", Zod.string().email())
}) { map ->
    User(
        name = map["name"] as String,
        email = map["email"] as String
    )
}

val result = userSchema.safeParse(mapOf("name" to "A", "email" to "invalid-email"))

when (result) {
    is ZodResult.Success -> {
        println("Valid data: ${result.data}")
    }
    is ZodResult.Failure -> {
        result.error.errors.forEach { error ->
            println("Validation error: $error")
        }
    }
}
A major correctness and API release with breaking changes. See the full changelog for the full list.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Structured ZodIssue errors with paths, codes, flatten() and ZodValidationException.
  • Result helpers (getOrNull, getOrThrow, map, fold).
  • Explicit coercion (Zod.coerce.*), Zod.lazy, JSON interop and Zod.date().
  • Typed refine() on string, number, boolean, array, set, object and date schemas.
  • toJsonSchema(), configurable error maps and @ZodModel KSP code generation.
  • Gradle 9.9.2, JDK 21 toolchain, Dokka, Kover, API compatibility checks and hardened CI.

docs.title: Code generation (KSP)
docs.text: zodkmp-ksp generates ZodObjectSchema definitions for annotated data classes, removing the manual { map -> User(...) } parser.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
plugins {
    id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.14"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("io.github.piashcse:zodkmp:2.0.0")
    ksp("io.github.piashcse:zodkmp-ksp:2.0.0")
}

For Kotlin Multiplatform, add the processor to the target that consumes the models. KSP2 does not expose a common-metadata task in this setup, so the processor runs per target:

dependencies {
    add("kspJvm", "io.github.piashcse:zodkmp-ksp:2.0.0")
    add("kspAndroid", "io.github.piashcse:zodkmp-ksp:2.0.0")
}

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import com.piashcse.zodkmp.ZodModel

@ZodModel(strict = true)
data class User(
    val name: String,
    val age: Int,
    val nickname: String?,
    val tags: List<String>,
)

val result = UserZod.schema.safeParse(input)

The processor generates <ClassName>Zod.schema in the same package.

docs.title: Supported types
docs.text:
• String, Int, Long, Double, Float, Boolean
  • enums
  • other @ZodModel classes
  • nullable variants of the above
  • List<T> of the above

Unsupported types produce a KSP warning and fall back to Zod.any(). @ZodModel(strict = true) rejects unknown keys.

docs.title: Arrays
docs.text:
Validate array values with constraints:

val stringArray = Zod.array(Zod.string())

// With constraints
val constrainedArray = Zod.array(Zod.string())
    .min(2, "Array must have at least 2 elements")
    .max(10, "Array must have at most 10 elements")
    .length(5, "Array must have exactly 5 elements")
    .nonempty("Array must not be empty")

docs.title: Tuples
docs.text:
Validate fixed-length arrays with specific types for each position:

val coordinates = Zod.tuple(listOf(Zod.number(), Zod.number()))

// Usage
val result = coordinates.safeParse(listOf(10.0, 20.0))

docs.title: Sets
docs.text:
Validate sets where every element matches an element schema:

val emailSet = Zod.set(Zod.string().email())
val positiveNumbers = Zod.set(Zod.number().positive())

// Usage
val result = emailSet.safeParse(setOf("a@b.com", "c@d.com")) // Success

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
Validate maps with separate key and value schemas:

val scores = Zod.map(Zod.string(), Zod.number())

// Usage
val result = scores.safeParse(mapOf("Alice" to 90.0, "Bob" to 85.0)) // Success

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
Validate objects with string keys and uniform value types:

val stringRecord = Zod.record(Zod.string())
val numberRecord = Zod.record(Zod.number())

// Usage
val userData = mapOf("name" to "John", "city" to "NYC")
val result = stringRecord.safeParse(userData)

docs.title: Key-Schema Records
docs.text:
Validate record keys against a schema:

val ipToName = Zod.record(Zod.string().ip(), Zod.string())

val result = ipToName.safeParse(mapOf("192.168.1.1" to "router")) // Success

docs.title: Loose Records
docs.text:
looseRecord validates that all values match, but does not reject keys that fail the key schema:

val looseIpRecord = Zod.looseRecord(Zod.string().ip(), Zod.string())

// Non-matching keys pass through without error, values are still validated
val result = looseIpRecord.safeParse(mapOf("192.168.1.1" to "router", "hostname" to "home"))
// Success — "hostname" does not match the key schema but is not rejected

docs.title: Strict Records
docs.text:
strictRecord rejects keys that fail the key schema:

val strictIpRecord = Zod.strictRecord(Zod.string().ip(), Zod.string())

val result1 = strictIpRecord.safeParse(mapOf("192.168.1.1" to "router")) // Success
val result2 = strictIpRecord.safeParse(mapOf("hostname" to "home"))      // Failure

docs.title: String Enums
docs.text:
Validate enum values:

// String enums
val roleSchema = Zod.enum("admin", "user", "guest")

// Using collections
val roles = listOf("admin", "user", "guest")
val roleSchema = Zod.enum(roles)

docs.title: Kotlin Enum Classes
docs.text:
Validate against a Kotlin enum class. The schema accepts both enum values and their names, and the result is the enum instance:

enum class Role {
    ADMIN,
    USER,
    GUEST
}

val roleSchema = Zod.enum(Role::class)

// Usage
val result1 = roleSchema.safeParse(Role.ADMIN)   // Success with Role.ADMIN
val result2 = roleSchema.safeParse("ADMIN")      // Success with Role.ADMIN
val result3 = roleSchema.safeParse("admin")      // Failure — names are case-sensitive
val result4 = roleSchema.safeParse("SUPERUSER")  // Failure

docs.title: Errors and results
docs.text:
safeParse returns a ZodResult. Failures contain a structured ZodError:

val result = schema.safeParse(input)

when (result) {
    is ZodResult.Success -> println(result.data)
    is ZodResult.Failure -> result.error.issues.forEach { issue ->
        println("${issue.path.renderPath()}: ${issue.message} [${issue.code}]")
    }
}

Each ZodIssue carries:

  • code: a ZodIssueCode such as INVALID_TYPE, INVALID_FORMAT, TOO_SMALL, TOO_BIG, NOT_MULTIPLE_OF, INVALID_UNION, UNRECOGNIZED_KEYS, REQUIRED or CUSTOM.
  • path: a list of ZodPathSegment.Property / ZodPathSegment.Index values.
  • message, plus optional expected / received / cause.

Paths render as address.city or tags[1]. ZodError.errors keeps the historical path-prefixed string list, and flatten() groups issues by top-level field:

val error = (result as ZodResult.Failure).error
val flattened = error.flatten()
// flattened["formErrors"], flattened["fieldErrors"]

docs.title: Throwing
docs.text:
parse and parseSuspend throw ZodValidationException, which exposes the ZodError:

try {
    val user = userSchema.parse(input)
} catch (e: ZodValidationException) {
    println(e.error.flatten())
}

docs.title: Result helpers
docs.text:
result.getOrNull()
result.getOrThrow()
result.map { transform(it) }
result.fold(onSuccess = { it }, onFailure = { it.issues.size })
result.isSuccess
result.isFailure

docs.title: Localized / custom messages
docs.text:
Set a process-wide error map to override messages by issue code, path or any other field:

ZodConfig.errorMap = { issue ->
    when (issue.code) {
        ZodIssueCode.REQUIRED -> "Campo obligatorio"
        ZodIssueCode.INVALID_TYPE -> "Tipo no válido"
        else -> null
    }
}

Returning null keeps the built-in message. Call ZodConfig.reset() in tests.

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
JsonElement values can be validated directly; objects and arrays are converted to plain Kotlin maps and lists:

val result = userSchema.safeParseJson(jsonObject)

docs.title: Intersections
docs.text:
Validate values that must satisfy multiple schemas:

val personSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Person>({
    string("name", Zod.string())
}) { map ->
    Person(name = map["name"] as String)
}

val employeeSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Employee>({
    string("employeeId", Zod.string())
}) { map ->
    Employee(employeeId = map["employeeId"] as String)
}

val personEmployeeSchema = Zod.intersection(personSchema, employeeSchema)

docs.title: Basic Object Validation
docs.text:
Validate complex objects:

val userSchema = Zod.objectSchema<User>({
    string("name", Zod.string().min(2))
    string("email", Zod.string().email())
    number("age", Zod.number().min(0.0).max(120.0))
    field("isActive", Zod.boolean().default(true))
}) { map ->
    User(
        name = map["name"] as String,
        email = map["email"] as String,
        age = map["age"] as Double,
        isActive = map["isActive"] as? Boolean ?: true
    )
}

docs.title: Strict Objects
docs.text:
Strict objects (reject unknown keys):

val strictUserSchema = Zod.objectSchema<User>({
    string("name", Zod.string().min(2))
    string("email", Zod.string().email())
}) { map ->
    User(
        name = map["name"] as String,
        email = map["email"] as String
    )
}.strict()

docs.title: Nested Object Validation
docs.text:
val addressSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Address>({
    string("street", Zod.string().min(5))
    string("city", Zod.string().min(2))
    string("zipCode", Zod.string().regex(Regex("\\d{5}"))
}) { map ->
    Address(
        street = map["street"] as String,
        city = map["city"] as String,
        zipCode = map["zipCode"] as String
    )
}

val userWithAddressSchema = Zod.objectSchema<UserWithAddress>({
    string("name", Zod.string().min(2))
    field("address", addressSchema)
}) { map ->
    UserWithAddress(
        name = map["name"] as String,
        address = map["address"] as Address
    )
}

docs.title: Pick
docs.text:
Create a new schema with only the selected keys:

val userSchema = Zod.objectSchema<User>({
    string("name", Zod.string())
    string("email", Zod.string().email())
    number("age", Zod.number())
}) { map -> /* ... */ }

val publicProfile = userSchema.pick("name", "age")
val result = publicProfile.safeParse(mapOf("name" to "John", "age" to 30)) // Success

docs.title: Omit
docs.text:
Create a new schema without the specified keys:

val credentialsOnly = userSchema.omit("name", "age")
val result = credentialsOnly.safeParse(mapOf("email" to "john@example.com")) // Success

docs.title: Partial
docs.text:
Make every field optional:

val updateUser = userSchema.partial()
val result = updateUser.safeParse(mapOf("email" to "new@example.com")) // Success

docs.title: Deep Partial
docs.text:
Make every field optional recursively, including nested objects, arrays and sets:

val settingsSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Settings>({
    field("profile", Zod.objectSchema<Profile>({
        string("displayName", Zod.string())
        string("bio", Zod.string())
    }) { map -> /* ... */ })
    field("tags", Zod.array(Zod.string()))
}) { map -> /* ... */ }

val updateSettings = settingsSchema.deepPartial()
val result = updateSettings.safeParse(mapOf("profile" to mapOf("displayName" to "Alex"))) // Success

docs.title: Merge
docs.text:
Combine two object schemas into one. Merged keys must not overlap:

val baseSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Base>({
    string("id", Zod.string())
}) { map -> /* ... */ }

val profileSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Profile>({
    string("name", Zod.string())
}) { map -> /* ... */ }

val combined = baseSchema.merge(profileSchema)
val result = combined.safeParse(mapOf("id" to "u1", "name" to "John")) // Success

and is an infix alias for merge:

val combined = baseSchema and profileSchema

docs.title: Extend
docs.text:
Combine two object schemas, allowing overlapping keys (the right-hand schema wins):

val extended = baseSchema.extend(profileSchema)

docs.title: Object Modes
docs.text:
Objects validate in strip mode by default (unknown keys are dropped). Switch modes:

// Reject unknown keys
val strictSchema = userSchema.strict()
val result1 = strictSchema.safeParse(mapOf("name" to "John", "unknown" to 1)) // Failure

// Keep unknown keys in the output
val passthroughSchema = userSchema.passthrough()
val result2 = passthroughSchema.safeParse(mapOf("name" to "John", "extra" to true)) // Success

// Drop unknown keys (default)
val stripSchema = userSchema.strip()

docs.title: String
docs.text:
Validate string values with various constraints:

val stringSchema = Zod.string()

// With constraints
val constrainedString = Zod.string()
    .min(5, "String must be at least 5 characters")
    .max(100, "String must be at most 100 characters")
    .email("Must be a valid email address")
    .url("Must be a valid URL")
    .regex(Regex("^[A-Za-z]+$"), "Must contain only letters")
    .startsWith("Hello", "Must start with 'Hello'")
    .endsWith("World", "Must end with 'World'")
    .includes("test", "Must contain 'test'")
    .trim()
    .toLowerCase()

// Checks run in declaration order. Lengths count Unicode code points.
val exactlyTen = Zod.string().length(10)

docs.title: String Formats
docs.text:
Validate common string formats:

val uuidSchema = Zod.string().uuid()
val ipv4Schema = Zod.string().ipv4()
val ipv6Schema = Zod.string().ipv6()
val ipSchema = Zod.string().ip()          // accepts IPv4 or IPv6
val emojiSchema = Zod.string().emoji()
val cuidSchema = Zod.string().cuid()
val cuid2Schema = Zod.string().cuid2()      // exactly 24 characters by default
val ulidSchema = Zod.string().ulid()
val nanoidSchema = Zod.string().nanoid()    // exactly 21 characters by default
val datetimeSchema = Zod.string().datetime()   // ISO-8601
val base64Schema = Zod.string().base64()
val base64urlSchema = Zod.string().base64url()

// Usage
val valid = uuidSchema.safeParse("123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000") // Success
val invalid = uuidSchema.safeParse("not-a-uuid")                          // Failure

docs.title: Number
docs.text:
Validate numeric values:

val numberSchema = Zod.number()

// With constraints
val constrainedNumber = Zod.number()
    .gt(0.0, "Must be greater than 0")
    .gte(5.0, "Must be greater than or equal to 5")
    .lt(100.0, "Must be less than 100")
    .lte(50.0, "Must be less than or equal to 50")
    .max(90.0, "Must be at most 90")
    .int("Must be an integer")
    .nonNegative("Must be non-negative")
    .multipleOf(0.5, "Must be a multiple of 0.5")
    .finite("Must be a finite number")

// Numeric strings require opt-in coercion:
Zod.number().safeParse("42")     // Failure
Zod.coerce.number().parse("42")  // 42.0

docs.title: Long
docs.text:
Validate 64-bit integers (the Kotlin analog of Zod's bigint):

val longSchema = Zod.long()
val positiveId = Zod.long().positive().max(1_000_000)

// Usage (accepts Long and integral numbers; strings require Zod.coerce.long())
val result1 = longSchema.safeParse(9223372036854775807L) // Success
val result2 = longSchema.safeParse(42)                    // Success
val result3 = Zod.coerce.long().safeParse("7")            // Success
val result4 = longSchema.safeParse(3.14)                  // Failure

docs.title: Boolean
docs.text:
Validate boolean values:

val booleanSchema = Zod.boolean()

// Strings require opt-in coercion:
Zod.boolean().safeParse("true")     // Failure
Zod.coerce.boolean().parse("true")  // true

docs.title: Date
docs.text:
Validate date values:

val dateSchema = Zod.date()

// With constraints
val constrainedDate = Zod.date()
    .min(LocalDateTime(2020, 1, 1, 0, 0), "Date must be after 2020")
    .max(LocalDateTime(2030, 12, 31, 23, 59), "Date must be before 2030")

// ISO-8601 strings require opt-in coercion:
Zod.coerce.date().parse("2023-01-01T12:00:00Z")

docs.title: Null & Undefined
docs.text:
Validate null and undefined values:

val nullSchema = Zod.nullType()
val undefinedSchema = Zod.undefined()

docs.title: Literals
docs.text:
Validate exact literal values:

val literalSchema = Zod.literal("admin")
val numberLiteral = Zod.literal(42)
val booleanLiteral = Zod.literal(true)

Literal accepts multiple values and returns a union of literals. A single value returns a plain ZodLiteral, and no values returns ZodNever:

val statusLiteral = Zod.literal("draft", "published", "archived")
val result1 = statusLiteral.safeParse("published") // Success
val result2 = statusLiteral.safeParse("deleted")   // Failure

docs.title: Any
docs.text:
Accepts any value without validation:

val anySchema = Zod.any()
val result = anySchema.safeParse(mapOf("anything" to listOf(1, 2, 3))) // Success

docs.title: Unknown
docs.text:
Accepts any value, but the result stays typed as Any?:

val unknownSchema = Zod.unknown()
val result = unknownSchema.safeParse("whatever") // Success

docs.title: Never
docs.text:
Rejects every value (useful to mark impossible branches):

val neverSchema = Zod.never()
val result = neverSchema.safeParse(42) // Failure

docs.title: Void
docs.text:
Accepts null values and returns Unit (mirrors Zod's z.void() which accepts undefined):

val voidSchema = Zod.void()
val result = voidSchema.safeParse(null) // Success with Unit

docs.title: InstanceOf
docs.text:
Validate that a value is an instance of a given class (reified, no reflection):

val dateSchema = Zod.instanceOf<Date>()
val urlSchema = Zod.instanceOf<URL>()

// Usage
val result1 = dateSchema.safeParse(Date())     // Success
val result2 = dateSchema.safeParse("2026-01-01") // Failure

docs.title: Nullables
docs.text:
Mark schemas as accepting null values:

val nullableString = Zod.string().nullable()

// Usage
val result1 = nullableString.safeParse("hello") // Success
val result2 = nullableString.safeParse(null)   // Success
val result3 = nullableString.safeParse(42)       // Failure

docs.title: Optionals
docs.text:
Mark schemas as accepting undefined values:

val optionalString = Zod.string().optional()

// Usage
val result1 = optionalString.safeParse("hello") // Success
val result2 = optionalString.safeParse(null)     // Success (undefined)

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
Provide default values for schemas:

val stringWithDefault = Zod.string().default("unknown")
val numberWithDefault = Zod.number().default { 0.0 }

// Usage
val result1 = stringWithDefault.safeParse(null)     // Success with "unknown"
val result2 = stringWithDefault.safeParse("hello")  // Success with "hello"

docs.title: Refinements
docs.text:
Add custom validation rules:

val evenNumber = Zod.number().refine({ it.toInt() % 2 == 0 }) { "Number must be even" }
val strongPassword = Zod.string().refine({ it.length >= 8 && it.any { char -> char.isDigit() } }) { "Password must be at least 8 characters with numbers" }

docs.title: Conditional Validation
docs.text:
// Custom validation based on other fields
val conditionalSchema = Zod.objectSchema<Conditional>({
    string("type", Zod.enum("email", "phone"))
    string("value", Zod.string())
}) { map ->
    Conditional(
        type = map["type"] as String,
        value = map["value"] as String
    )
}.refine({ obj ->
    when (obj.type) {
        "email" -> obj.value.contains("@")
        "phone" -> obj.value.all { it.isDigit() || it == '-' }
        else -> true
    }
}) { "Value must match the selected type" }

docs.title: Suspend Refinements
docs.text:
Run asynchronous validation rules (e.g. database or network checks). Requires kotlinx-coroutines-core:

val uniqueUsername = Zod.string()
    .min(3)
    .refineSuspend({ username ->
        userRepository.isAvailable(username) // suspend call
    }) { "Username is already taken" }

// Usage from a coroutine
suspend fun check(username: String): Boolean {
    val result = uniqueUsername.safeParseSuspend(username)
    return result is ZodResult.Success
}

The sync parse and safeParse methods throw IllegalStateException on a schema that contains suspend refinements; use safeParseSuspend/parseSuspend instead. safeParseSuspend/parseSuspend are available as defaults on every schema, so they work with regular schemas too.

docs.title: Transformations
docs.text:
Transform values during validation:

val uppercaseString = Zod.string().transform { it.uppercase() }
val toString = Zod.number().transform { it.toInt().toString() }

// Usage
val result = toString.safeParse(42.5) // Success with "42"

docs.title: Preprocess
docs.text:
Transform the input before validating it with the wrapped schema:

val trimAndValidate = Zod.string().trim().preprocess { value ->
    (value as? String)?.trim()
}

val numFromString = Zod.preprocess({ (it as? String)?.toDoubleOrNull() }, Zod.number())
val result = numFromString.safeParse("42.5") // Success with 42.5

preprocess is also available as an extension on any schema.

docs.title: Catch
docs.text:
Return a fallback value when validation fails:

val withDefault = Zod.string().catch("unknown")

// Or compute the fallback from the invalid input
val lengthOrDefault = Zod.string().catch { input -> input?.toString()?.length ?: 0 }

val result1 = withDefault.safeParse(null)    // Success with "unknown"
val result2 = withDefault.safeParse("hello") // Success with "hello"

docs.title: Pipe
docs.text:
Validate the output of one schema with another schema:

val stringToNumber = Zod.pipe(Zod.string(), Zod.number())
// Or: Zod.string().pipe(Zod.number())

val result = stringToNumber.safeParse("42.5") // Success with 42.5

docs.title: Describe & Meta
docs.text:
Attach a description or metadata to a schema without changing validation:

val userSchema = Zod.string()
    .describe("The user's full name")
    .meta(mapOf("kind" to "name", "required" to true))

// Access the metadata
val describe = userSchema as ZodDescribe<*>
println(describe.description) // "The user's full name"
println(describe.metadata)    // {kind=name, required=true}

docs.title: Basic Unions
docs.text:
Validate values that match any of multiple schemas:

val stringOrNumber = Zod.union(Zod.string(), Zod.number())
val complexUnion = Zod.union(
    Zod.string(),
    Zod.number(),
    Zod.objectSchema<Point>({
        number("x", Zod.number())
        number("y", Zod.number())
    }) { map ->
        Point(
            x = map["x"] as Double,
            y = map["y"] as Double
        )
    }
)

docs.title: Discriminated Unions
docs.text:
discriminatedUnion maps objects into a sealed class hierarchy. The literal value of a discriminator key selects which object schema is applied:

sealed class Animal {
    data class Dog(val name: String, val goodBoy: Boolean) : Animal()
    data class Cat(val name: String, val lives: Double) : Animal()
}

val animalSchema = Zod.discriminatedUnion<Animal>(
    discriminator = "type",
    Zod.objectSchema<Animal.Dog>({
        field("type", Zod.literal("dog"))
        string("name", Zod.string())
        boolean("goodBoy", Zod.boolean())
    }) { map ->
        Animal.Dog(map["name"] as String, map["goodBoy"] as Boolean)
    },
    Zod.objectSchema<Animal.Cat>({
        field("type", Zod.literal("cat"))
        string("name", Zod.string())
        number("lives", Zod.number())
    }) { map ->
        Animal.Cat(map["name"] as String, map["lives"] as Double)
    }
)

val result = animalSchema.safeParse(mapOf("type" to "dog", "name" to "Rex", "goodBoy" to true))
// Success with Animal.Dog

discriminatedUnion is also available with a list of options:

val animalSchema = Zod.discriminatedUnion<Animal>("type", listOf(dogSchema, catSchema))

The discriminator key should be declared with Zod.literal(...) on each option. If no literal matches the input value, the schema falls back to trying each option in order and returns the first that parses successfully.
